source_text:
Τέρτιος ὁ κατ' αὐτὴν τὴν πρὸς Ῥωμαίους ἐπιστολὴν τοῦ Παύλου γράψας
ἐπίσκοπος δεύτερος Ἰκονίου ἐγένετο.
μβʹ. Ἔραστος, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ μέμνηται Παῦλος ἐν τῇ αὐτῇ ἐπιστολῇ, οἰκονόμος
τῆς ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις ἐκκλησίας ἐγένετο, ἔπειτα ἐπίσκοπος Πανεάδος ἐγένετο.
μγʹ. Φύγελος, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ ὁ Παῦλος μέμνηται ὡς ἑτεροδοξήσαντος καὶ τὰ
Σίμωνος φρονήσαντος, ἐπίσκοπος Ἐφέσου γέγονεν.
μδʹ. Ἑρμογένης, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ ὁ Παῦλος ὁμοίως ὡς ἑτεροδοξήσαντος
μέμνηται, ἐπίσκοπος ἐν Μεγάροις ἐγένετο.
μεʹ. ∆ημᾶς, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ ὁμοίως ὁ ἀπόστολος Παῦλος μέμνηται ὡς
ἀποστήσαντος· δηλοῖ γὰρ περὶ τῶν τριῶν ἐν τῇ πρὸς Τιμόθεον δευτέρᾳ αὐτοῦ
ἐπιστολῇ, ὅτι ἑτεροδοξήσαντες Φύγελος καὶ Ἑρμογένης ἀντέστησαν τῇ διδασκαλίᾳ
αὐτοῦ. Ὁ δὲ ∆ημᾶς ἀγαπήσας τὸν νῦν αἰῶνα κατέλιπε τὸν εὐαγγελικὸν λόγον, καὶ ἐν
Θεσσαλονίκῃ ἱερεὺς τῶν εἰδώλων ἐγένετο. Περὶ τούτων καὶ Ἰωάννης ὁ ἀπόστολος
ἔγραψεν· ἐξ ἡμῶν ἐξῆλθον, ἀλλ' οὐκ ἦσαν ἐξ ἡμῶν.
μς ʹ. Κούαρτος, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ ἐν τῇ πρὸς Ῥωμαίους ἐπιστολῇ ὁ Παῦλος
μέμνηται, ἐπίσκοπος Βηρυτοῦ ἐγένετο.
124 μζʹ. Ἀπολλώς, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ ἐν τῇ πρὸς Κορινθίους ἐπιστολῇ ὁ Παῦλος
μέμνηται, ἐπίσκοπος Καισαρείας ἐγένετο.
μηʹ. Κηφᾶς, ὃν ὁ ἀπόστολος Παῦλος ἐν Ἀντιοχείᾳ ἤλεγξε διαλεχθεὶς
ὁμωνυμοῦντα τῷ Πέτρῳ, ἐπίσκοπος Κονίας ἐγένετο.
μθʹ. Σωσθένης, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ ὁ Παῦλος μέμνηται, ἐπίσκοπος Κολοφονιάδος
ἐγένετο.
νʹ. Ἐπαφρόδιτος, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ ὁ Παῦλος μέμνηται, ἐπίσκοπος Ἀδριακῆς
ἐγένετο. ναʹ. Καῖσαρ, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ ὁ Παῦλος μέμνηται, ἐπίσκοπος ∆υῤῥαχίου
ἐγένετο.
νβʹ. Μάρκος ὁ ἀνέψιος Βαρνάβα, οὗ καὶ ὁ Παῦλος μέμνηται, ἐπίσκοπος
Ἀπολλωνιάδος ἐγένετο.
νγʹ. Ἰωσὴφ ὁ λεγόμενος καὶ Ἰοῦστος καὶ Βαρσαββᾶς, οὗ μέμνηται Λουκᾶς ἐν
ταῖς πράξεσι τῶν ἀποστόλων ὡς συγκληρωθέντος τῷ Ματθίᾳ, ἐπίσκοπος
Ἐλευθεροπόλεως γέγονε.
νδʹ. Ἀρτεμᾶς, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ ὁ Παῦλος μέμνηται, ἐπίσκοπος ἐν Λύστρᾳ
ἐγένετο.
νεʹ. Κλήμης, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ ὁ Παῦλος μέμνηται, λέγων· μετὰ Κλήμεντος καὶ
τῶν λοιπῶν συνεγρῶν μου, ὃς καὶ πρῶ125 τος ἐξ ἐθνῶν καὶ Ἑλλήνων ἐπίστευσεν εἰς
Χριστόν, ἐπίσκοπος Σαρδικῆς ἐγένετο.
νς ʹ. Ὀνησίφορος, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ ὁ Παῦλος μέμνηται, ἐπίσκοπος Κορωνείας
ἐγένετο.
νζʹ. Τυχικός, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ μέμνηται ὁ Παῦλος, πρῶτος ἐπίσκοπος
Χαλκηδόνος τῆς ἐν Βιθυνίᾳ ἐγένετο.
νηʹ. Κάρπος, οὗ καὶ αὐτοῦ ὁ Παῦλος μέμνηται, ἐπίσκοπος Βεῤῥοίας τῆς
Θρᾴκης ἐγένετο. νθʹ.
thought_title: Later disciples as bishops with heresy and desertion noted
orientation: Epiphanius continues his catalogue of the seventy disciples, naming the city where each served as bishop.
pass_a_gloss: Tertius, the one who wrote at the time of the letter to the Romans of Paul, became second bishop of Iconium. 42. Erastus, whom also himself Paul mentions in the same letter, became steward of the church in Jerusalem, then became bishop of Paneas. 43. Phygelus, whom also himself Paul mentions as having fallen into heresy and having held the mind of Simon, became bishop of Ephesus. 44. Hermogenes, whom also himself Paul likewise mentions as having fallen into heresy, became bishop in Megara. 45. Demas, whom also himself likewise the apostle Paul mentions as having apostatized; for he makes clear concerning the three in his second letter to Timothy, that having fallen into heresy Phygelus and Hermogenes stood against his teaching. And Demas having loved the present age left behind the gospel word, and in Thessalonica became priest of idols. Concerning these also John the apostle wrote: they went out from us, but they were not of us. 46. Quartus, whom also himself in the letter to the Romans Paul mentions, became bishop of Beirut. 47. Apollos, whom also himself in the letter to the Corinthians Paul mentions, became bishop of Caesarea. 48. Cephas, whom the apostle Paul in Antioch rebuked after having held discussion, being of same name with Peter, became bishop of Conia. 49. Sosthenes, whom also himself Paul mentions, became bishop of Colophonias. 50. Epaphroditus, whom also himself Paul mentions, became bishop of Adriake. 51. Caesar, whom also himself Paul mentions, became bishop of Dyrrachium. 52. Mark the cousin of Barnabas, whom also Paul mentions, became bishop of Apollonias. 53. Joseph the one called both Justus and Barsabbas, whom Luke mentions in the Acts of the Apostles as having been chosen by lot together with Matthias, became bishop of Eleutheropolis. 54. Artemas, whom also himself Paul mentions, became bishop in Lystra. 55. Clement, whom also himself Paul mentions, saying: with Clement and the rest of my fellow workers, who also first from Gentiles and Greeks believed in Christ, became bishop of Sardica. 56. Onesiphorus, whom also himself Paul mentions, became bishop of Coronea. 57. Tychicus, whom also himself Paul mentions, became first bishop of Chalcedon the one in Bithynia. 58. Carpus, whom also himself Paul mentions, became bishop of Beroea the one of Thrace. 59.

lemmas.gloss: having been chosen by lot together with

choices.why: Work brief glossary fixes this term to fall into heresy
Source distinguishes Demas from the two who fell into heresy; aorist of revolt and desertion, stronger than falling away
Literal household manager sense for the Jerusalem church office
Keeps literal genitive of idol, not pagan temple in general

pass_b_english: 41. Tertius, who wrote Paul's letter to the Romans, became the second bishop of Iconium. 42. Erastus, whom Paul also mentions in the same letter, became steward of the church in Jerusalem, and afterward became bishop of Paneas. 43. Phygelus, whom Paul also mentions as having fallen into heresy and shared Simon's views, became bishop of Ephesus. 44. Hermogenes, whom Paul likewise mentions as having fallen into heresy, became bishop in Megara.

45. Demas, whom the apostle Paul likewise mentions as having apostatized, abandoned the faith. For in his second letter to Timothy Paul speaks about all three: Phygelus and Hermogenes fell into heresy and opposed his teaching, but Demas loved this present world and abandoned the gospel message (2 Timothy 4:10), and became a priest of idols in Thessalonica. About such people John the apostle also wrote, "They went out from us, but they did not belong to us" (1 John 2:19).

46. Quartus, whom Paul also mentions in his letter to the Romans, became bishop of Beirut. 47. Apollos, whom Paul also mentions in his letter to the Corinthians, became bishop of Caesarea. 48. Cephas, whom the apostle Paul rebuked in Antioch and who shares his name with Peter, became bishop of Conia. 49. Sosthenes, whom Paul also mentions, became bishop of Colophonias. 50. Epaphroditus, whom Paul also mentions, became bishop of Adriake. 51. Caesar, whom Paul also mentions, became bishop of Dyrrachium. 52. Mark, the cousin of Barnabas, whom Paul also mentions, became bishop of Apollonias. 53. Joseph, also called Justus and Barsabbas, whom Luke mentions in the Acts of the Apostles as the one put to the lot alongside Matthias, became bishop of Eleutheropolis.

54. Artemas, whom Paul also mentions, became bishop in Lystra. 55. Clement, whom Paul also mentions when he says, "with Clement and the rest of my fellow workers" (Philippians 4:3), became bishop of Sardica. He was the first from the Gentiles and the Greeks to believe in Christ. 56. Onesiphorus, whom Paul also mentions, became bishop of Coronea. 57. Tychicus, whom Paul also mentions, became the first bishop of Chalcedon in Bithynia. 58. Carpus, whom Paul also mentions, became bishop of Beroea in Thrace.

problems.quote: as the one chosen by lot with Matthias
problems.why: συγκληρωθέντος means put to the lot alongside, not chosen by lot; in Acts 1:23-26 Joseph was balloted with Matthias, and only Matthias was chosen.
problems.fix: as having been put to the lot alongside Matthias

edits.old: as the one chosen by lot with Matthias
edits.new: as the one put to the lot alongside Matthias

fixed: Fixed 'as the one chosen by lot with Matthias': source ὡς συγκληρωθέντος τῷ Ματθίᾳ means balloted/put to the lot together with Matthias as a candidate, not chosen — only Matthias was chosen.

last_rejected.why: 2 Timothy 4:10 speaks of deserting Paul, not abandoning the gospel.
last_rejected.fix: Demas loved this present world (2 Timothy 4:10), abandoned the gospel message, and became a priest of idols in Thessalonica.
last_rejected.ruling: Source cites 2 Timothy and echoes 4:10 (ἀγαπήσας τὸν νῦν αἰῶνα), adapting it with κατέλιπε τὸν εὐαγγελικὸν λόγον; reference is accurate.
